plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled, dark branches burst into delicate five-petaled blossoms while winter still grips the landscape. The flowers give off a sweet, spicy perfume. Ume groves at shrines and parks are among the first signs of spring in Japan.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, with peak bloom usually from mid-February to early March
plants.location: Japan, especially the plum groves (bairin) at shrines such as Tokyo's Kameido Tenjin
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are traditionally linked with the scholar Sugawara no Michizane, which is why they are planted so often at Tenmangu shrines across Japan.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, pure-white bells with green-tipped inner petals push up through cold ground on slender, silvery-green leaves. In February they carpet woodlands, riverbanks and churchyards in drifts of white.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with the main display in February
plants.location: Woodlands, gardens and roadsides across the United Kingdom and Ireland
plants.funFact: Snowdrops are so closely tied to the end of winter that their flowering dates are recorded as a signal of the changing seasons.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.commonName: Agapanthus (African lily, lily of the Nile)
plants.description: Tall, leafless stems rise from clumps of strappy green leaves. Each one carries a rounded burst of funnel-shaped blue flowers. In the southern summer they line driveways and fill sunny borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly November to February in the Southern Hemisphere summer, with the last flowers fading in late summer
plants.location: Gardens in southern Australia and New Zealand, where it is widely grown
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, agapanthus is not a true lily. It is native to southern Africa, and its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
